note: S434 - EMPIRICAL TEST of my own step-61 prediction that a low-volatility nightly layer would fail. I tested it rather than relying on the prediction, because the eternal-death rule requires measurement and a forecast is not evidence.
what_i_predicted_in_step61: Removing the top volatility quartile buys roughly +0.6pp, taking lift to about 2.6pp, still below the 4.0 floor, while cutting n from 1807 to about 1355 inflates perm_sd to ~1.00 and raises the z bar.
control_note: Control sampled at 50k eligible bars per step 46, run WITH trailing and break-even per BUG-NULLUNCOND. natr is lagged by shift(1) so the filter uses only information through the signal bar.

prediction_scoring.verdict: CORRECT in conclusion, WRONG in magnitude - the filter helped MORE than I forecast (+1.67pp rather than +0.6pp), yet the conclusion holds because 3.621 < 4.0.
prediction_scoring.why_i_under_predicted: I estimated the lift gain from the AUC alone, treating filter selectivity as uniform across the volatility distribution. In fact the top-quartile trades are much worse than AUC 0.477 implies, so shallow removal is more productive than a linear reading of AUC predicts. This is a real limitation of using AUC to forecast filter yield, and it is exactly why the test was worth running rather than trusting the forecast.
prediction_scoring.honesty_note: Recording that my forecast erred in the layer's FAVOUR matters: had I skipped the test on the strength of my own prediction, I would have missed that the true best lift is 3.62pp - only 0.38pp from the floor - a materially different picture from 2.6pp and much closer to viable.

self_defeating_dynamic_observed_directly.finding: This is the clearest empirical demonstration of the step-41 arithmetic in the whole mission.
self_defeating_dynamic_observed_directly.reading: Lift improves 86% from unfiltered to best-filtered, yet z improves only 32% and then FALLS, because perm_sd inflates 40% over the same range. The filter's statistical benefit is almost entirely cancelled by the cost of the trades it discards. At 25% retention both collapse: lift falls to 2.044 because the filter has begun removing WINNERS, and z falls to 1.20 because n=471 nearly doubles perm_sd.
self_defeating_dynamic_observed_directly.why_this_matters_beyond_S434: Step 54 correctly identified that SHALLOW filtering escapes the self-defeating dynamic in principle. This measurement shows the escape window is NARROW and bounded in practice: favourable between 100% and 75% retention, neutral by 50%, destructive by 25%. Any future mission closing a lift deficit with a filter should expect a usable window of roughly 10-30% removal and must track the z trajectory, not just the lift trajectory.

verdict: All four arms FAIL H3. The best is 'keep bottom 50% natr' at lift 3.621pp against the 4.0pp floor - 91% of the bar, the closest any variant in this entire mission has come - but it fails on BOTH criteria simultaneously: lift is 0.379pp short AND z at 2.97 is below the 3.09 floor. The two failures are COUPLED, not independent: closing the lift gap requires deeper filtering, which inflates perm_sd further and pushes z DOWN. There is no retention level at which both clear.
no_further_search_conducted: I did not sweep other volatility indicators, other quantile thresholds, or combinations, and I state why: it would inflate n_trials against myself while the measured z trajectory shows the route is structurally bounded rather than merely untuned. Sweeping until something passes at z~3.1 with n~900 would be precisely the mass-search behaviour H5 exists to catch.
